source_snapshot.items: Boot Order - Set boot option to Disk
source_snapshot.procedure: Verify four BIOS settings, set EFI disk boot via IPMI, read bootparam 5, restart, confirm Disk boot and BIOS option; note about 60-second flag clear.
source_snapshot.criteria: Node boots from Disk and option matches setting.
source_snapshot.script: Private bootorder_set_boot_option_to_disk.sh; 10 attended and 30 machine minutes; source requests log clearing.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL Redfish Once/Hdd PATCH and reboot with TLS bypass, inline credentials and a guessed generic disk target.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at HIGH risk; exact EFI disk mapping, protected one-time override, reboot observation, auto-clear and persistent BootOrder protection.

historical_reviews.deepseek: It recognizes state change but guesses Hdd, omits source BIOS checks and cannot prove which EFI entry booted, the clear timing or unchanged persistent order.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly binds the override to an approved same-SUT disk entry, limits it to Once and requires console/OS identity plus recovery.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: A generic Hdd selector can choose a different physical disk or firmware entry than intended. Acceptance needs bootloader/root-device evidence tied to the approved EFI entry, while one-time flag consumption and persistent BootOrder are separate postconditions.

original_test_intent: Set a one-time EFI Disk boot override on the approved node, prove the intended disk actually boots, verify the override clears in the accepted window and protect the persistent normal BootOrder.
original_method: Record exact node/BMC/BIOS and EFI disk identity, inspect the source BIOS prerequisites and existing order, set only the supported protected Once disk override, read back Redfish/IPMI boot parameters, reboot with human approval, identify the disk from console/OS, observe flag clearing, and verify BootOrder and health are restored.
manual_activity: The owner identifies the intended EFI disk and approves reboot; an operator watches POST/console, prevents recovery/installer entry and owns recovery and verdict.
required_inputs: Intended physical disk, EFI entry, bootloader and OS/root-device mapping
Meaning of source PXE/HTTP BIOS prerequisites
Independent console/PDU recovery and protected credentials
safety_requirements: Stop on wrong disk, recovery/installer, persistent flag or timeout
Preserve logs and filesystem health evidence
Clear/restore through the approved recovery path and never auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify target and EFI disk mapping
Set/read approved one-time override after authorization
Poll flag consumption and compare persistent order
engineer_actions: Approve EFI disk target and BIOS interpretation
Observe console and intervene on wrong path

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A Once override is directionally correct, but Hdd is unverified, TLS/secrets are unsafe and the command omits BIOS prerequisites, exact EFI identity, clear timing and persistent-order checks.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Resolve the supported selector for the approved EFI disk, use protected one-time set/readback, reboot only after approval and verify boot identity, flag consumption and unchanged BootOrder through independent evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 10/30-minute estimates, BIOS checks, reboot and 60-second +/-10% claim remain, subject to vendor confirmation; logs are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a before/write/readback/POST/OS/clear ledger that binds the selected override to EFI entry, bootloader, disk serial or stable ID and root device, and diffs persistent BootOrder before and after.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes generic disk guessing and adds deterministic boot identity, bounded recovery and order preservation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: PATCH success and bootparam output do not prove the intended disk executed or that the flag cleared safely.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware may map Hdd to first enumerated storage rather than a named EFI entry; vendor schema and platform order must govern the selector.

project_override_considerations: The Project must explain the PXE/HTTP BIOS prerequisites for a Disk test or treat them only as preserved read-only prechecks. Any required BIOS enablement needs a separate approved change/restore plan.
expected_evidence: Approved exact target, EFI/disk identity, BIOS prerequisite and normal-order baseline
Protected one-time override write and Redfish/IPMI readback
POST/console and OS proof of the intended disk/bootloader/root device
Unchanged persistent BootOrder, OS/filesystem/BMC health and preserved logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, procedure and criteria consistently target Disk boot. PXE/HTTP BIOS settings are questionable prerequisites but are explicitly preserved as checks and do not direct a different boot target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Exact disk mapping, schema, BIOS interpretation, reboot window and recovery are normal inputs; execution blocks only if these cannot be resolved safely or the intended disk is unavailable.

review_improvement: Turns a guessed generic Hdd override into an identity-bound one-time boot with explicit flag consumption, order protection and wrong-path recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: Firmware boot target classes are not unique device identities. On multi-disk systems, Hdd may select whichever entry enumerates first, so a successful reboot can still test the wrong asset. Correlating EFI entry, bootloader and OS root device is essential, and verifying that the transient flag clears without changing BootOrder prevents the test from leaving a latent service failure.
